(18 February 2017) | average attendance = 6,980{{cite web|url=http://www.slstat.com/spl2016-2017en/allstat.php?id=11|title=Attendance|publisher=Saudi Pro League Statistics|access-date=14 August 2016}} | prevseason = [[2015–16 Saudi Professional League|2015–16]] | nextseason = [[2017–18 Saudi Professional League|2017–18]] | updated = 4 May 2017 }} The '''2016–17 Saudi Professional League''' (also known as the '''Jameel League''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 41st season of [[Saudi Pro League]], the top Saudi professional league for association football clubs, since its inception in 1976. The season started on 11 August 2016 and concluded on 4 May 2017.{{cite web|url=http://www.aljleague.com/news/details/abdul-latif-jameel-league-2016-2017/|title=اتحاد الكرة يحدد موعد انطلاق دوري عبداللطيف جميل 2016-2017|work=ALJleague.com|language=ar|date=4 May 2016|access-date=11 May 2016}} [[Al Hilal SFC|Al-Hilal]] won their fourteenth league title, and first since the [[2010–11 Saudi Professional League|2010–11 season]], with two matches to spare following a 2–1 win over [[Al Shabab FC (Riyadh)|Al-Shabab]] on 20 April.{{cite web|url=http://www.the-afc.com/saudi-arabia/al-hilal-seal-saudi-pro-league-title|title=Al Hilal seal Saudi League title|publisher=Asian Football Confederation|work=the-afc.com|date=20 April 2017|access-date=11 May 2017}} The defending champions were [[Al-Ahli Saudi FC|Al-Ahli]]{{cite web|url=http://www.the-afc.com/afc-champions-league-2016/al-ahli-down-al-hilal-to-seal-saudi-league-crown|title=Al Ahli down Al Hilal to seal Saudi League crown|publisher=Asian Football Confederation|work=the-afc.com|date=25 April 2016|access-date=11 May 2016}} who finished as runners-up. [[Al-Ettifaq FC|Al-Ettifaq]] and [[Al Batin FC|Al-Batin]] entered as the two promoted teams from the [[2015–16 Saudi First Division]]. ==Teams== The league comprises 14 teams, 11 from the [[2015–16 Saudi Pro League|2015–16 campaign]], as well as two teams promoted from the [[2015–16 Saudi First Division|2015–16 First Division]] and the [[2015–16 Saudi Pro League#Relegation play-offs|relegation play-off]] winners. On the final day of the season [[Al-Mujazzal FC|Al-Mojzel]] won the First Division title and their first-ever promotion to the top flight after a 3–2 win against [[Al Jeel FC|Al-Jeel]].{{cite web|title=المجزل والاتفاق إلى جميل وهبوط الرياض والنهضة|trans-title=Al-Mojzel and Al-Ettifaq to the Pro League, Al-Riyadh and Al-Nahda were relegated|url=http://www.thesaff.com.sa/NewsDetails.aspx?NewsID=14344|language=ar|work=thesaff.com.sa|publisher=Saudi Arabian Football Federation|date=23 April 2016|access-date=11 May 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160505164813/http://www.thesaff.com.sa/NewsDetails.aspx?NewsID=14344|archive-date=5 May 2016|url-status=dead}} [[Al-Ettifaq FC|Al-Ettifaq]] were also promoted after they finished in 2nd place, it would be their first participation in the Pro League since the [[2013–14 Saudi Pro League|2013–14 season]]. The two promoted teams replaced [[Najran SC|Najran]] and [[Hajer FC|Hajer]]. [[Al Raed FC|Al-Raed]] were relegation play-off winners.{{cite news|url=http://www.alriyadh.com/1506598|title=الرائد برباعية في مرمى الباطن يضمن بقاءه في دوري جميل|publisher=Al-Riyadh|language=ar|date=26 May 2016|access-date=28 May 2016}} On 3 August 2016, Al-Mojzel were stripped of their title and instead got relegated to the Second Division due to a [[Match fixing in association football|match fixing]] scandal. The [[Saudi Arabian Football Federation|SAFF]] decided to promote [[Al Batin FC|Al-Batin]] instead.{{cite web|url=http://www.thesaff.com.sa/NewsDetails.aspx?NewsID=14469|title=الانضباط تقرر تهبيط المجزل للدرجة الثانية|language=ar|work=thesaff.com.sa|publisher=Saudi Arabian Football Federation|date=21 July 2016|access-date=10 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160819212121/http://www.thesaff.com.sa/NewsDetails.aspx?NewsID=14469|archive-date=19 August 2016|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=http://www.thesaff.com.sa/NewsDetails.aspx?NewsID=14496|title=بيان: صعود الباطن لدوري جميل وبقاء النهضة بالأولى|language=ar|work=thesaff.com.sa|publisher=Saudi Arabian Football Federation|date=3 August 2016|access-date=10 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160819210314/http://www.thesaff.com.sa/NewsDetails.aspx?NewsID=14496|archive-date=19 August 2016|url-status=dead}} ===Stadiums and locations===
